senses.gloss:
Haya denotes ‘horse’ in the Rigveda and later.
Foot notes v. 46, 1; vii. 74, 4; ix. 107, 25.
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, vii. 47; xxii. 19, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 231.

Hāyana denotes a ‘year,’ usually in compounds. In the kāṭhaka Saṃhitā and the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa the term appears as a designation of a species of red rice. As an adjective in the sense of ‘lasting a year’ or ‘recurring every year,’ it is applied to fever in the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes Av. viii. 2, 21; śata-hāyana, ‘a hundred years old,’ viii. 2, 8; 7, 22; hāyanī, xii. 1, 36 (probably corrupt).

v. 3, 3, 6 (the taittirīya Saṃhitā, i. 8, 10, 1, has instead mahā-vrīhi, ‘great rice’).
